caveats: n=4 per cell: the interaction standard error is roughly double that of a main effect, so only large differential responses are detectable

steps.question: Which genes show a drug response in KO that differs from the drug response in WT — i.e. a non-zero genotype:treatment interaction — and what are the simple drug effects within WT and within KO separately?
constraints: The interaction term must be tested directly as a model coefficient — do not infer 'different drug effect' by intersecting or differencing two separately-run marginal DE gene lists

Do not filter genes a second time; use the T1S1 filtered set so the multiple-testing burden is fixed and stated

steps.description: Fit DESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment on the filtered counts, with WT and vehicle as reference levels. Extract, as the primary result, the interaction coefficient genotypeKO:treatmentdrug with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, applying LFC shrinkage (ashr, which supports arbitrary coefficients) for ranking only — significance calls come from the unshrunken Wald test. Then, from the same fitted model, extract the four interpretable simple contrasts: drug vs vehicle within WT, drug vs vehicle within KO, KO vs WT within vehicle, and KO vs WT within drug. Report, for the interaction, the number of genes at FDR < 0.05 and at FDR < 0.1, an MA plot, a volcano plot, and the top 30 interaction genes with their per-cell normalised mean expression across all four condition groups so the shape of the interaction (antagonised, amplified, reversed, or qualitative) can be read directly. Cross-tabulate the interaction hits against the two within-genotype simple drug effects, and classify each into: drug-responsive in WT only, KO only, both with differing magnitude, or opposite direction. Explicitly report the dispersion-estimate plot and the number of genes flagged as outliers by Cook's distance. State in the results summary that with n=4 per cell the interaction contrast has substantially lower power than a main effect, so an empty or short interaction list is not evidence of no genotype-dependent drug action.

plan.title: KO x drug interaction DE in brain bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is exactly the genotype:treatment interaction term of a 2x2 factorial. The inputs are a 12,000-gene x 16-sample salmon-derived gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, 17 columns = gene ID + 16 samples) and a 16-row metadata table carrying genotype (WT, KO), treatment (vehicle, drug), and a combined condition label, with n=4 per cell. The plan therefore centres on one properly specified DESeq2 model, ~design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, with the interaction as the primary contrast (T1S2), rather than on comparing two separately-run marginal DE lists — a difference of significance is not a significant difference. Before modelling, T1S1 loads and QC-checks the matrix: sample-name concordance between the two files, integer-count check (salmon output may carry non-integers; the profile explicitly does not say whether length correction was applied, so the step must inspect and round if needed and record that it did), library-size and detection-rate summary, VST + PCA/correlation clustering coloured by genotype, treatment and cell, and independent filtering. n=4 per cell gives modest power for an interaction term (the interaction SE is roughly twice that of a main effect), so T1S2 must report the marginal simple effects (drug-vs-vehicle within WT and within KO, genotype effect within each treatment) alongside the interaction to make the direction of any modulation interpretable, and must state the power limitation explicitly rather than reporting an empty interaction list as evidence of no modulation. T1S3 tests the same interaction question at the pathway level, where aggregating across gene sets recovers power the per-gene test lacks, using human hallmark and GO-BP gene sets (organism matches: taxon 9606) against the interaction-statistic ranking. T2S1 runs an independent confirmation of the interaction term with limma-voom on the same design, so the headline claim does not rest on a single distributional assumption; concordance between the two is the honest measure of robustness at this sample size.
